concepts.title: Nitrogenous Wastes and Modes of Excretion
concepts.definition: Animals eliminate ammonia, urea or uric acid as nitrogenous wastes, and accordingly are classified as ammonotelic like most aquatic organisms, ureotelic like mammals and terrestrial amphibians, or uricotelic like reptiles, birds and insects that conserve water.
concepts.key_idea: Ammonia is the most toxic form needing large water for elimination, uric acid is the least toxic and excreted as pellets, which explains why aquatic forms are ammonotelic while desert birds are uricotelic.

concepts.title: Human Excretory System and the Nephron
concepts.definition: The human excretory system has a pair of kidneys with about a million nephrons each, ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra; each nephron has Bowman's capsule with a glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, with cortical and juxtamedullary types.
concepts.key_idea: The juxtaglomerular apparatus of macula densa and juxtaglomerular cells regulates glomerular filtration, and malpighian corpuscles lie in the cortex while loops of Henle run into the medulla.

solution_steps.explain: Follow kidney, ureter, bladder and urethra in order.

concepts.title: Urine Formation: Glomerular Filtration Rate and Reabsorption
concepts.section: 16.3 Mechanism of Concentration of the Filtrate
concepts.definition: Urine formation involves glomerular filtration where about 1200 ml of blood is filtered per minute producing a glomerular filtration rate of about 125 ml per minute or 180 litres per day, tubular reabsorption returning nearly 99 per cent of the filtrate, and tubular secretion; the final urine is only about 1.5 litres a day.
concepts.key_idea: Comparing 180 litres of filtrate a day with 1.5 litres of urine shows that nearly 99 per cent of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules, chiefly in the proximal convoluted tubule.
question_patterns: what is the gfr of a healthy person and what does it mean
how much blood do the kidneys filter per minute
calculate the percentage of filtrate reabsorbed per day
compare the daily filtrate with daily urine output
describe the steps of urine formation
what substances are reabsorbed in the pct

solution_steps.explain: Divide the glomerular filtration rate by the blood filtered per minute and multiply by 100 to get the filtrate percentage

concepts.title: Counter Current Mechanism and Hormonal Control
concepts.section: 16.4 Counter Current Mechanism, 16.5 Regulation of Kidney Function
concepts.definition: The counter current mechanism of Henle's loop and the vasa recta, with the medullary gradient rising to about 1200 mOsmol per litre in the inner medulla, concentrates the filtrate, while ADH, aldosterone and the juxtaglomerular apparatus with renin regulate water and ion balance.
concepts.key_idea: ADH increases water reabsorption from the collecting duct and aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption, so small changes in their secretion adjust the volume and concentration of urine.

solution_steps.explain: Follow filtrate in Henle's loop and blood in vasa recta in opposite directions.

concepts.title: Micturition, Disorders of the Excretory System and Dialysis
concepts.definition: The neural signalling of micturition releases urine from the bladder when it is full, and disorders include uremia, renal calculi and glomerulonephritis; haemodialysis with a cellophane tube in dialysing fluid removes urea from the blood of uremic patients, and a kidney transplant is the ultimate remedy.
concepts.key_idea: In haemodialysis blood from an artery passes through cellophane tubes in dialysing fluid and is returned to a vein, clearing nitrogenous wastes that failed renal clearance.
